result.title: Accounting Policy Manual - posting authority, support, approvals
result.text:
HALVARD SYSTEMS - ACCOUNTING POLICY MANUAL (excerpt), effective 2026-01-01
Applies to Halvard Systems Inc. (US), Halvard Systems Ltd (UK), Halvard Systems GmbH (DE).

1. Posting authority. Senior accountants may post manual journal entries up to USD 10,000
   per entry (local-currency entries are measured at the month-end rate of the entry month).
   Any entry above USD 10,000 must be routed to the Controller with an approval request
   (request_approval) immediately after posting; it remains pending until approved.
   Splitting one transaction into several entries to stay under the threshold is prohibited.
2. Support. Every journal entry must have its supporting document(s) attached. An entry
   without support is not a valid entry.
3. Capitalization. Individual equipment purchases of USD 2,500 or more (local-currency
   equivalent at the month-end rate) are capitalized to 1500 Computer Equipment and
   depreciated over 36 months beginning the month after acquisition.
4. Prepaids. Payments covering services or events in future periods (more than one month
   out, or spanning more than one month) above USD 1,000 are recorded as prepaid (1210
   Prepaid Software for software, 1220 Prepaid Insurance for insurance, 1200 Prepaid Expenses
   for everything else, including deposits for future events) and expensed straight-line over
   the coverage period starting the month coverage begins, or when the event occurs.
5. Accruals. Expenses are recorded in the period the goods or services are received. Services
   received but not yet invoiced at month-end are accrued to 2100 Accrued Expenses using the
   best available evidence (vendor statements, approved timesheets, engagement terms).
   Quotes or proposals for future work are not liabilities.
6. Revenue. Revenue is recognized under ASC 606 per the contract terms. Deferred revenue
   (2200) is released as performance obligations are satisfied. Usage earned but not yet
   invoiced is recorded to 1300 Unbilled Receivables.
7. Customer credits. SLA credits are issued only per contract terms and verified uptime data
   (see the monthly uptime report). Credits are recorded as a reduction of the related revenue.
8. Cash application. Customer receipts are applied to invoices per remittance advice. Receipts
   that cannot be matched to an open invoice remain in 2950 Unapplied Cash.
9. FX. Monetary balances denominated in a currency other than the entity's functional
   currency are remeasured at the month-end rate; gains/losses go to 6950 FX Gain/Loss.
   Intercompany charges are recorded by the receiving entity at the month-end rate of the
   month charged.
10. Payroll. Returned payroll deposits are recorded to 2150 Accrued Payroll & Unclaimed
   Wages until reissued. Unpaid wages at month-end are accrued to 2150.
11. Exceptions. Items that cannot be supported must be reported via flag_exception. Never
   post an entry to force a reconciliation or to make balances agree.
12. Periods. January and February 2026 are closed. March 2026 is open.

args.text:
MEMO — March 2026 Revenue Recognition: Dunmore Foods & Harlow Freight (US entity)
Prepared by: david.murguia@gmail.com | Date: 2026-04-03 | Period: 2026-03 (open)

=====================================================================
1. DUNMORE FOODS — JE-00311, 2026-03-31, USD 5,000
   DR 2200 Deferred Revenue      5,000
     CR 4000 Subscription Revenue      5,000
   Support: DOC-0002 (Subscription Agreement), DOC-0155 (Amendment No.1),
            DOC-0005 (INV-1001), DOC-0156 (INV-1052)
=====================================================================

Component A — Core platform subscription: USD 4,000
  Per DOC-0002: USD 48,000/yr, term 2026-01-01 to 2026-12-31, invoiced annually in
  advance, "service is provided evenly over the term." This is a single performance
  obligation satisfied ratably over time (ASC 606-10-25-27). 48,000 / 12 = 4,000/month.
  Consistent with JE-00111 (Jan) and JE-00215 (Feb), both 4,000.

Component B — Analytics module: USD 1,000
  KEY JUDGMENT — contract modification analysis (ASC 606-10-25-10 through 25-13):
  Amendment No.1 (DOC-0155, effective 2026-03-01) adds the Analytics module for
  2026-03-01 to 2026-12-31 at USD 1,000/month (USD 10,000 total), invoiced in advance.
  The amendment states on its face that the Analytics module is (i) a DISTINCT service
  and (ii) priced at its STANDALONE SELLING PRICE, and that core subscription terms
  are unchanged.

  Both conditions in ASC 606-10-25-12 are therefore met, so the modification is
  accounted for as a SEPARATE CONTRACT. Consequences:
    - NO reallocation of transaction price to the remaining core subscription. The
      core obligation continues to be recognized at its original 4,000/month; the
      prospective "blended rate" approach under 606-10-25-13(a) does NOT apply here.
    - NO cumulative catch-up adjustment (that would only apply if the remaining
      goods/services were not distinct — 606-10-25-13(b)).
  The 10,000 is recognized ratably over the 10-month service period 2026-03-01 to
  2026-12-31 = 1,000/month. March is the first month: 1,000.

  Note on what was NOT done: the full 10,000 invoiced on 2026-03-01 was correctly
  deferred by billing (JE-00229, DR 1100 / CR 2200). Recognizing the invoice in full
  in March would overstate March revenue by 9,000; the cash/invoice timing does not
  drive recognition (ASC 606-10-45-1/2).

  March total = 4,000 + 1,000 = 5,000.

Deferred revenue roll-forward check (account 2200, US) — TIES EXACTLY:
  Opening 3/1: 50,000 cr  →  less JE-00311 5,000  →  closing 45,000 cr
  Expected Dunmore balance at 3/31:
    Core:      9 remaining months (Apr–Dec) x 4,000 = 36,000
    Analytics: 9 remaining months (Apr–Dec) x 1,000 =  9,000
    Total                                            = 45,000  ✓

=====================================================================
2. HARLOW FREIGHT — JE-00312, 2026-03-31, USD 5,000
   DR 1300 Unbilled Receivables (Contract Asset)  5,000
     CR 4100 Usage Revenue                              5,000
   Support: DOC-0001 (Usage Agreement), DOC-0206 (March usage report)
=====================================================================

  Per DOC-0001: USD 0.10 per shipment processed, no minimum, and "Halvard's
  performance obligation is satisfied as each shipment is processed." Usage is
  invoiced quarterly in arrears, with the Q1 invoice issued in early April.

  DOC-0206: 50,000 shipments processed in March 2026.
  50,000 x USD 0.10 = USD 5,000.

  Because the obligation is satisfied as shipments are processed, revenue is earned in
  March even though no invoice has been issued at 3/31. Per policy manual §6, usage
  earned but not yet invoiced is recorded to 1300 Unbilled Receivables (contract asset,
  not a receivable, since the right to consideration is not yet unconditional pending
  the quarterly billing event). This is the variable-consideration-allocation practical
  approach in ASC 606-10-55-65 / 606-10-32-40: the per-shipment rate corresponds
  directly to the value transferred each month, so no estimation or constraint is needed.
  Treatment is consistent with JE-00112 (Jan) and JE-00210 (Feb).

Unbilled receivables roll-forward check (account 1300, US) — TIES EXACTLY:
  Jan  41,200 shipments x 0.10 =  4,120  (JE-00112)
  Feb  44,800 shipments x 0.10 =  4,480  (JE-00210)
  Mar  50,000 shipments x 0.10 =  5,000  (JE-00312)
  Q1 total 136,000 shipments   = 13,600  = 1300 ending balance 13,600 ✓
  This agrees to the Q1 invoice to be issued to Harlow Freight in early April; the
  contract asset should reclassify to 1100 AR at that point.

=====================================================================
3. POLICY / CONTROLS
=====================================================================
  - Support: both entries have supporting documents attached (policy §2). ✓
  - Posting authority (policy §1): each entry is USD 5,000, below the USD 10,000
    senior-accountant limit, so no controller approval request was required. These are
    two economically separate transactions (different customers, different performance
    obligations, different revenue accounts) — this is not a prohibited split of a single
    transaction to stay under the threshold. The Dunmore core and Analytics components
    were deliberately combined into a single 5,000 entry rather than split.
  - Both entries dated 2026-03-31 in the open March period (policy §12).
  - No SLA credits were identified for either customer for March (policy §7); no uptime
    report indicating a qualifying outage was located, so no revenue reduction was booked.
  - No exceptions were flagged: both items are fully supported by executed contracts and
    source usage/invoice documentation.

=====================================================================
4. CHECKLIST STATUS
=====================================================================
  US "Revenue recognition" set to IN_PROGRESS, not complete. My assignment covered only
  Dunmore Foods and Harlow Freight. The revenue accountant should confirm that remaining
  US customers (Acme Logistics, Corvid Retail, Beacon Health, Evergreen Bank, Fairview
  Labs, etc.) and the UK/DE entities' March revenue have been recognized before the item
  is closed. Note that after JE-00311 the entire remaining US deferred revenue balance of
  45,000 is attributable to Dunmore, which suggests other US customers are billed monthly
  with revenue recognized on invoice — worth a confirming review.
